heroHeadline: Rubin Observatory Returns to Engineering Work After Two-Month Storm Recovery
heroSubtitle: NSF NOIRLab reported on Sep 11 that its Coquimbo Region mountain facilities are operational again, nearly two months after a historic mid-July winter storm cut road access, power, and water to Cerro Pachón and Cerro Tololo. Vera C. Rubin Observatory has transitioned from storm recovery into previously scheduled engineering downtime; the SOAR and Blanco telescopes nearby have resumed science observations. Before the storm, the survey had logged over 11,000 new asteroids and ~380 trans-Neptunian objects, and analysis of Early Data Preview 2 yielded the survey's first confirmed extragalactic find, the ultra-faint dwarf galaxy Aquarius IV. A second EDP2 data phase remains due Q4 2026.
